units: mm (URDF applies scale 0.001, same as dual_rb3_730e)
why: The hulls OVER-APPROXIMATE the stand, so the guard reports the arm closer to it
than it is -- padding stacked on top of d_hard_m, in the safe direction but paid
for out of usable workspace. Measured 2026-09-10 with tools/stand_hull_sweep.py:
1500 random arm poses in the 10..150 mm arm<->stand band, each variant's reported
clearance compared against a reference model built from the SOURCE STL as a coal
BVH (exact distance) -- the same 'measure against the source STL, never the hulls'
rule the 2026-09-06 mount calibration used.
20 hulls / thr 0.08 (previous): err mean 0.11, p95 0.03, MAX 10.82 mm
40 hulls / thr 0.03 (this):     err mean 0.05, p95 0.09, MAX  5.97 mm
The padding is negligible in the mean and lives entirely in the tail, which is
what a floor has to cover: 10.8 mm was 36% of the 30 mm d_hard_m, 6.0 mm is 20%.
Neither set ever under-approximates (err_min -0.03 mm = GJK/BVH tolerance).
COST, and why not finer. Per-eval time scales with the pair count; the ratio was
measured on the same poses and applied to the live distribution (servo_log
60 hulls 1.76x -> p99 2.20 ms | 78 hulls 2.06x -> p99 2.57 ms (err max 2.44 mm)
40 is the finest set whose p99 stays under the 2 ms servo tick. That bound is not
about the 500 Hz loop -- the monitor is async and the loop never waits on it -- it
is about the monitor still producing one verdict PER TICK. Past 2 ms it evaluates
every other tick, which doubles the interval swept_samples has to cover (1.2 ->
2.4 mm of motion at the 0.6 m/s ceiling) and raises verdict age into the latency
compensation. 60/78 hulls buy 2.4-3.6 mm more accuracy and are worth revisiting if
d_hard_m is ever lowered, but then swept_samples has to be looked at with them.
Reproducible: coacd 1.0.14 with the parameters below (default seed) regenerates
these 40 hulls bit-identically; verified 2026-09-10.
